notes: STATUS. Every one of the thirteen functions byte-matches the cartridge, but this entry cannot be promoted today and deliberately stays text-verified. Two independent tree-level defects block it, both recorded below; neither is a property of this reconstruction and neither was worked around.

Destructor form. The cartridge emits _ZN9dScDSMT_cD1Ev at ov007:0x020cc028 BELOW _ZN9dScDSMT_cD0Ev at 0x020cc070. Under the pinned mwccarm 2004/b56 with default (deferred) codegen that order is reproduced by defining the destructor INLINE IN CLASS (virtual ~dScDSMT_c() {} in include/dScDSMT_c.h); the out-of-line form emits D0 ahead of D1 and adds a homeless D2. The header was changed from the out-of-line declaration to the inline definition as part of this work, and tubuild verify confirms the result: "all 13 function(s) in the expected ROM-ascending section order".

Key function. Because the destructor is inline it cannot be the key function; _ZN9dScDSMT_c13InitResourcesEv -- the first declared non-inline virtual -- is, and defining it here is what emits _ZTV9dScDSMT_c and, through slots 16/17, the D1/D0 pair. It therefore cannot be dropped from this TU: without it the destructor pair is not emitted at all.

BLOCKER 1 -- _ZTVN9dScDSMT_c15graphCallback_cE has no configured ROM home. The object emits the nested class's 0x18-byte vtable (its key function, GraphCallback0, is defined here), and the symbol resolves to nothing in any config/**/symbols.txt. It can therefore take neither compiler-only disposition: deadstrip-data is refused for want of a home, and a plain deadstrip is refused outright for an _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV record. The cartridge DOES hold the record -- ov007:0x021032a8 storage, 0x021032b0 address point -- proved by the RTTI word at 0x021032ac being 0x02103284 == _ZTIN9dScDSMT_c15graphCallback_cE, and by the 0x18 span 0x021032a8..0x021032c0 matching the emitted symbol's size exactly. config/arm9/overlays/ov007/symbols.txt carries it only under the placeholder name data_ov007_021032b0. This entry consequently has 13 of the 14 compiler_only_output rows it needs and tubuild verify ends in PROMOTION REFUSED.

BLOCKER 2 -- overlay_100 / overlay_102 do not link. Behavior and InitResources each pass an overlay id as (int)&overlay_100 / (int)&overlay_102. The spelling is load-bearing: the cartridge loads both from the literal pool (ldr r0,[pc,#0x74] -> 0x020cc450 = 0x64 and ldr r0,[pc,#0x70] -> 0x020cc454 = 0x66), and writing the plain constants instead compiles to mov and loses eight bytes (0x188 against the cartridge's 0x190 -- measured with tools/match.py, MATCHING VERSIONS: none). But config/arm9/symbols.txt puts overlay_100 and overlay_102 at 0x00000064 and 0x00000066, addresses that fall outside every module's sections, so no delinked gap object defines them: `dsd check symbols` already reports both as "not found in linked binary" on a stock tree, and marking either function `complete` makes mwldarm fail the link outright -- "Undefined : overlay_100 ... Referenced from dScDSMT_c::InitResources() / dScDSMT_c::Behavior()" (measured: tubuild linkcheck --baseline --module ov007 with the two entries enrolled). tools/eligible.py calls both functions ELIGIBLE, which is the known case of rule 5 greenlighting a link mwldarm refuses. This is why the queue row shows unmatched:2, and it is not fixable in source.

Why there is no partial promotion. Behavior is ordinal 10 and InitResources ordinal 12 of 13 in ROM-ascending order, with CleanupResources between them, so no contiguous sub-range can drop them and keep the rest. Dropping InitResources also removes the key function, and with it the emission of ordinals 0 and 1 (D1/D0). The next sub-range down that emits no key function at all is 0x020cc118..0x020cc2cc -- four functions, two of them unattributed helpers -- which is not worth a boundary. The legacy spelling in this TU is the defined one (overlay_100 / overlay_102, the names config/arm9/symbols.txt actually carries and the ones the legacy InitResources already used), not the overlay_64 / overlay_66 that the legacy Behavior used and that nothing defines.
